To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reliability of software systems can be improved by: (a) using a formal language for specifying requirements; (b) using a structured design method for designing the system; (c) using a structured programming language for implementing the system; (d) using a formal method for proving the correctness of the system; and (e) using a formal specification language for specifying the system.

(i) a software system can only be as reliable as the process of its development; (ii) the process of development should be a formalized process that can be verified for completeness and correctness, and (iii) the information that is passed between the different phases should be in a form that can be easily verified.

(1) the requirements analysis phase should be done by using the structured analysis method, and the design and implementation phases should be done by the structured design and structured programming methods, respectively, (2) the requirements analysis and design should be done by a team of experts and the implementation phase by a programmer who is not an expert, (3) a software system can only be reliable if the requirements are correct, the design is correct and complete, the implementation is correct and complete.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology for the construction of reliable software systems.
the design of a methodology for software development that will minimize the number of software errors that occur in a software system when it is being developed.
the design and implementation of a methodology of software engineering that can be used for the development of reliable software systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methodology presented in this paper is a practical and useful one for the development of reliable small software systems and computer programs.
the methodology presented in this paper can be used to improve the reliability of software systems.
the methodology of software development presented in this paper can be used to improve the reliability of a program or software system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a software system is reliable if it satisfies the following conditions: (1) The system is correct, (2) The system satisfies all its requirements, (3) The system is complete, and (4) The system is maintainable.
we are able to show that a methodology of software engineering that can improve the reliability of a system can be developed by examining the process of software development itself.
the methodology presented here is a good way of developing reliable software systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reliability of software systems is not a property that can be added to the system at the end of its development.
the reliability of a system can be improved if the development process is improved.
the process of software development is as important as the software itself.
